claims.claim: The house style rests on the Chicago Manual of Style 16th ed. and Merriam-Webster's Collegiate 11th ed., with the guide covering only D&D-specific departures.
claims.source: Wizards of the Coast, D&D Style Guide v1.04a
claims.quote: The Chicago Manual of Style, 16th edition

claims.claim: Rules text is written in the second person, which the guide presents as the standard way to achieve gender neutrality; singular 'they' is banned outside dialogue and 'he/she' alternation is forbidden.
claims.source: Wizards of the Coast, D&D Style Guide v1.04a
claims.quote: achieve gender neutrality by writing in the second person

claims.claim: Shank's MA thesis characterises campaign-setting handbooks as giving encyclopedic knowledge of D&D geography, history and politics alongside ancillary rules.
claims.source: Nathan Shank, 'The Narrative Structures of Dungeons and Dragons', MA thesis 2011 (academia.edu, abstract/intro only)
claims.quote: encyclopedic knowledge of D&D geography, history, and politics

claims.claim: Delta dates the first boxed text in a Gygax adventure to the 1982 published Lost Caverns of Tsojcanth.
claims.source: Delta (Daniel R. Collins), 'Early Evolution of Encounter Text', Delta's D&D Hotspot, 2021
claims.quote: And hey, there's boxed text for the first time!
claims.page: section '1982 - Lost Caverns of Tsojcanth Publication'

claims.claim: Gygax's 1974 Castle Greyhawk notes gave a single curt bullet-line per encounter area.
claims.source: Delta (Daniel R. Collins), 'Early Evolution of Encounter Text', 2021
claims.quote: only a single curt bullet-line per encounter area

claims.claim: Ray Winninger's First Rule of Dungeoncraft is never to force yourself to create more than you must.
claims.source: Ray Winninger, Dungeoncraft, Dragon 256 (later WotC's D&D executive producer)
claims.quote: Never force yourself to create more than

claims.claim: Winninger tells the DM to give the home settlement a rumour mill, a place where adventurers gather to swap boasts, rumours and legends.

claims.claim: Winninger sets the minimum population of a home base at two interesting NPCs, arguing it is better to develop two really good ideas than four or five mediocre ones.
claims.source: Ray Winninger, Dungeoncraft, Dragon 261, Interesting NPCs
claims.quote: better to develop two really good ideas than four
claims.routeHint: collected PDF at textual.ru, pypdf extraction

claims.claim: Christopher Perkins, then editor of DUNGEON Adventures, says Warriors of Heaven does not embrace the narrative style of most Planescape products because it is a core AD&D product.
claims.source: Christopher Perkins, interviewed at Planescape: I am the Mimir, 1999
claims.quote: does not embrace the narrative style of most PLANESCAPE

claims.claim: Waterdeep: Dragon Heist, the 2018 city adventure, credits Michele Carter, Scott Fitzgerald Gray and Kim Mohan as its editors.
claims.source: Waterdeep: Dragon Heist (Wizards of the Coast, 2018), credits page, read through the Internet Archive's OCR text
claims.quote: Editors: Michele Carter Scott Fitzgerald Cray, Kim Mohan

claims.claim: Jeremy Crawford is credited as managing editor of Waterdeep: Dragon Heist.
claims.source: Waterdeep: Dragon Heist (Wizards of the Coast, 2018), credits page, read through the Internet Archive's OCR text

claims.claim: A read-through of the 2014 Dungeon Master's Guide names Random Settlements as a section of its chapter 5.
claims.source: Lex Starwalker, Game Master's Journey episode 235, 16 Dec 2018

claims.claim: The same read-through names Mapping a Settlement as another section of the 2014 guide's chapter 5.

claims.claim: The same designer says he builds his human surnames on roots from western European cultures.

verdicts.trueWording: The Chicago Manual of Style, 16th edition
verdicts.note: SUPERSEDED - verbatim in the v1.04a guide they cite; the 2019 v1.08a reverses the rule; cite as history only. R11 finding 2, re-ordered by the chair at 04:36 (r13 item 4; asked in r9, r10 and r12): CONTRADICTED is wrong for a rule that was true of its edition.
verdicts.unsupportedLimb: none - the quoted Chicago-16th foundation is verbatim in v1.04a; the row is edition-bound, not false, and must carry the SUPERSEDED mark (v1.08a rests on Chicago 17th)

verdicts.trueWording: In rules text, we often achieve gender neutrality by writing in the second person.
verdicts.note: SUPERSEDED - verbatim in the v1.04a guide they cite; the 2019 v1.08a reverses the rule; cite as history only. R11 finding 2, re-ordered by the chair at 04:36 (r13 item 4; asked in r9, r10 and r12): CONTRADICTED is wrong for a rule that was true of its edition.
verdicts.unsupportedLimb: none - the quoted second-person/gender-neutrality rule and the singular-'they' ban are verbatim in v1.04a; the row is edition-bound, not false, and must carry the SUPERSEDED mark (v1.08a allows singular 'they')

verdicts.note: R13 REGRADE (chair ruling 04:36, item 5): BLOCKED, not NOT_FOUND - the direct fetch 403s (WebFetch and curl) and the only reachable page is a login-walled academia.edu listing whose body text is metadata and download prompts, so the thesis text was never read. verdicts.trueWording: And hey, there's boxed text for the first time!
verdicts.note: R13 REGRADE (r12 critic; chair ruling 04:36): PARTIAL on the unsupported limb, per the verifier's own note - "'First' is first within Delta's declared sample - adventures authored by Gygax at two-year intervals across 1974-1985." The quoted line ('And hey, there's boxed text for the first time!') and the 1982 Tsojcanth attribution are verbatim and stand.
verdicts.unsupportedLimb: the 'first boxed text in a Gygax adventure' limb: first only within Delta's declared sample of Gygax adventures taken at two-year intervals 1974-1985, not first absolutely

verdicts.trueWording: only a single curt bullet-line per encounter area
verdicts.note: R13 REGRADE (r12 critic; chair ruling 04:36): PARTIAL on the unsupported limb, per the verifier's own note - "Two hedges the claim drops: the notes were never published (known from a photo taken at a Gen Con 2007 event), and Delta records debate over whether the encounter text is original, with the map dated 'could be 1972-1974 or so'." The quoted phrase 'only a single curt bullet-line per encounter area' is verbatim.
verdicts.unsupportedLimb: the 1974 Castle Greyhawk figure: the claim drops the source's two hedges - the notes were never published (known only from a Gen Con 2007 photograph) and their authenticity/dating is debated on the page itself
